_note: The Matabele ant, Megaponera analis (M8 step 1c, docs/DESIGN.md 'Matabele colony, details'). Castes: the ergatoid (wingless) queen, and the workers, majors and minors on one continuous size spread (real Megaponera: one worker caste whose sizes run from about 5 to 18 mm, monophasic, Longhurst and Howse 1979; no soldiers, every worker raids and stings). Founding is colony_fission: a real queen never founds alone, a colony splits in two with a new queen (M9); until then a summoned queen starts an empty colony that spawn-egg workers near her join, or /antcolonies matabele <workers> makes one whole (the user's pick, 2026-10-24). So there is no founding section: a queen alone is never sealed in, digs nothing and lays nothing. nest.dug false: no planned nest is dug; the shallow nest (step 1d, MatabeleNest) is the best site within 32 blocks, a dead termite mound first, then under a fallen log, else the ground (a shaft and two rooms 3 and 5 down), and the workers dig only to open and join its spaces (the queen digs nothing); a room still holding dead comb is taken once it has rotted away. Hunger is on from the start (the user's pick, 2026-10-24): a colony whose prey pile (step 1e) runs empty goes hungry and starves; worker: slow after 2 days without a meal, dead after 4 (my picks, to confirm; real colonies raid termites 2 to 4 times a day and keep no store, so a colony cut off from termites dies fast); the queen dies after starve_ticks wanting food (5 days, my pick), but never while she is alone (a queen with no workers counts as founding). The brood numbers wait for the nest (1d). colony.max_workers 2500, the top of a real colony (400 to 2,500); real_cap and crew 50 as the termites. food: they eat only termites, from the prey pile (step 1e, the colony part prey_pile: stung, paralysed termites in the queen's room, a layer about 10 termites, rotten after a day and carried out to a heap beside the entrance; stocked by /antcolonies prey until the raids exist); the items tag is empty, no plants, the store's heap block an unused stand-in (they keep no store); worker.diet: young and old eat from the prey pile (nurse_food), one layer makes workers_per_piece 10 meals, one termite per ant a day (the user's pick, 2026-10-24), no mouth-to-mouth feeding (real Megaponera larvae are laid on the prey and eat it themselves, the queen eats from the pile); forage_at is empty: they stay in the nest (real Megaponera leave it only to raid, by day, step 4; my pick, 2026-10-24). refuse: a dead ant's body crumbles after corpse_decay_ticks (the dead are carried home in step 5).
_parts_note: prey_pile (M8 step 1e): the colony's food, termites in the queen's room, the nurses' food too. nest_defence (M8 step 2e): the colony stings a player who provokes it (the defence section). raids (M8 step 3): the scouts (3a, the raids.scouting section) and the raid columns (3b, the raids.column section).

worker_sizes._note: The real size spread of Megaponera workers (Longhurst and Howse 1979, from head widths: about half the workers majors, a quarter in between, a quarter minors; majors about 15 mm long, minors 9 to 11, the whole spread 5 to 18; the user's pick 'real count', 2026-10-24). Each new worker rolls its length from groups (share, the shortest, the commonest, the longest; a triangle between them), keeps it for life (saved) and is drawn at that length: with the major's model (made for major_model_mm) or the minor's (minor_model_mm), whichever its length is nearer (by ratio), scaled from it. The minor model is half the major's (2:1), so a real 10 mm minor is drawn a third bigger than the minor model.

colony._far_note: numbers_when_far true (M8 step 3f, 2026-11-05): a loaded Matabele colony with no player within 64 blocks (kept to 80) lives as numbers like every far colony (colony.AwayLife); its raids go on out of sight (raids.away, colony.RaidsAway), so a far colony raids, eats and grows as one in sight.

worker._rest_in_rooms_note: With nothing to do the workers go down into the nest's rooms and stay there, never in the shaft (real Megaponera crowd into their chamber with the queen and the brood; the user's report 2026-10-24: they piled up at the top of the chimney).

body_language._note: Personality ranges all open (as before 1c, when the ant read the termites' numbers); no hot ground or noticing yet (naps and cleaning since M8 step 3Q, below).
body_language._idle_note: M8 step 3Q, rest first (SpeciesProfile.Idle; real: about 40 percent of a colony's workers do nothing at any moment and some idle most of their lives, Charbonneau and Dornhaus 2015, 2017; Megaponera crowd the brood chamber between raids, Yusuf 2026). An ant with nothing to do stands, antennae moving, and strolls about strolls_per_minute times a minute (a calm one a quarter of it, the most restless 1.75 times) stroll_blocks (from, to) far; staying in, it settles within settle_within blocks of the queen's room (with the prey pile) and walks there first when farther. My picks, to confirm.
body_language._rest_note: M8 step 3Q, naps and cleaning (my picks, to confirm). naps: real ants sleep in many short naps (fire ant workers about 250 a day of about a minute, queens fewer and longer, Cassill et al. 2009); the harvester's numbers, the queen's naps longer; only inside the nest. groom: an idle ant now and then cleans one antenna, or both one after the other (both_share), with the front leg of its side, then the leg in its jaws (Farish 1972). allogroom: now and then it cleans a resting nestmate within reach blocks for ticks (from, to); ants do it far less than termites.

fight._note: M8 step 2a, the shared fight system (fight.FightNumbers). Health and damage per body, my picks, to confirm in the user's first fight test (the numbers the bodies had in code before): a major 10 health (two to four soldier bites; real majors seldom die in a raid, minors more often), a minor 5, the queen 20. Damage only counts on what it does not hunt (a chicken; the player comes in step 2e): on termites, its prey, every blow is a paralysing sting that pricks for half a point and never kills (fight.Fights). prey: Macrotermes, the termites it lives on.
fight._legs_note: M8 step 2d: majors and minors can have legs bitten off by termite soldiers (the chance is the soldier's leg_cut in macrotermes.json); the queen keeps hers until 2e gives her a fight.
fight._look_over_note: M8 fight polish, round A: after felling a termite the ant stands over it, its antennae on it, this long (the shortest and longest, ticks: 1 to 2 s, my pick, to confirm), then turns to the next; one termite at a time, each blow played to its end (real raids: the attack at a feeding site lasts 5 to 30 minutes, Yusuf 2026).
fight._give_up_note: M8 fight polish, round B: with no termite in reach the ant searches round the feeding spot, antennae down, this long (ticks: 2 minutes, my pick, to confirm) before its fight is over (real raids: the attack lasts 5 to 30 minutes, the ants searching the opened galleries and the ground, Yusuf 2026).
fight._clamped_note: M8 step 2c, a termite soldier clamped on a leg (the user's calls 2026-10-25; Frank et al. 2017: the worst handicap measured, the ant crawling home; nestmates took the termites off in 9 cases in 10, the leg kept): slowing, a living soldier on the leg slows it this share (75 percent), it fights no more and goes home; head_slowing, a dead head left locked on slows it 10 percent and it may fight again; care_ticks, a nestmate in the nest works this long (30 s) to take it off; clean, the chance the leg is kept (9 in 10, else the leg comes off with it). slowing, head_slowing and care_ticks are my picks, to confirm.
fight._rescue_note: M8 step 5, rescue and wound care (entity.Wounds, RescueGoal, WoundCareGoal; RaidColumn fetches its own hurt). Real Megaponera (Frank et al. 2017, 'Saving the injured'; Frank et al. 2018, wound treatment; Frank et al. 2023, antimicrobial treatment of infected wounds): a raider hurt in the fight (a termite clamped on, or 1 or 2 legs gone) calls for help with a smell from its head; nestmates pull the termites off and carry it home in the pupal pose; ants with 5 legs gone do not call and are left; at home nestmates lick the wound; untreated, 80 percent of the hurt die within a day, treated about 10; an infected wound changes the ant's smell about 11 hours after, and nestmates then dab the secretion of their metapleural gland on it, cutting deaths from about 90 to about 20 percent. help_reach: a nestmate hears the call this far (blocks); call_legs_max, carry_legs_max: with at most this many legs gone it calls and is carried (4: the game's crippled ant of 3 or 4 legs gone is carried too, my pick; 5 or 6 never happen in the game); field_pull_ticks: pulling a clamped termite off out in the field (10 s); lick_ticks, licks: each lick of a fresh wound and how many it gets; dab_ticks: each dab of gland secretion; infect_ticks: when it is settled whether the wound is infected (6,000 ticks, 6 game hours, time to be carried home and licked); infect_untended, infect_licked: the chance of infection with no lick, and after every lick; smell_ticks: an infected wound smells after this long (11,000 ticks, 11 game hours); course_ticks: an infected wound kills or heals by this long after (36,000, a day and a half); death_untreated, death_treated: the chance it kills, with no dab and with one; heal_ticks: a clean wound closes after this long (a game day; till then the ant rests and does not raid). Times on the TIME scale (a game day a real day); the chances real, the times my picks from the papers' hours, to confirm.

raids._scale_note: Raid rework R8, one scale for real distances (docs/DESIGN.md, 'R8, one scale, as built'). Three scales: GROUND, a block a metre, for the land (how far from the nest, where the termites feed): scouting.most_range 96 (the real foraging range of about 95 m, Yusuf 2026; real raids mostly much nearer, rich sites taken farther out, Frank and Linsenmair 2017), first_range, settled_range, range_step, search.find_margin, search.step and stay_least, mound_clue (notice, past_foot, ring_step), hours_and_sound.squeak_hear and edge_look, defence.reach; and on the termites' side the galleries' 50, the dead tree 10 to 30 past the mound's foot and the mounds every 96, all real Macrotermes distances in metres. BODY, a major about a block (a real major 15 to 18 mm), for ant to ant and ant to termite: column.spacing, abreast and stop_short, choosing.inspect_from, trails.cast_reach (a gap of a few ant lengths), RaidColumn's pick reach 1.6. TIME, a game day a real day (72 times faster): trails' 29 hours, the raid and scouting hours, the hunger days. The scales agree on speed: a major walks 2.5 blocks a second, 1.7 body lengths a second on the body scale, and on the ground and time scales 2.5 m in 72 real seconds, 3.5 cm a second, both a real walking ant's pace. Between the scales, game stretches kept on purpose (real ants smell termites only centimetres off, so on the ground scale they would never find a feeding spot): scouting.smell 5, search.scent 12, carry.collect_reach 10, spread_reach 8 and spread_see 5, sized to a feeding spot (a dead tree's mud, a few blocks). column.stop_short 4: the real column halts 20 to 50 cm short, under a block on the ground scale and 13 to 33 on the body scale; 4 kept, just outside the termites' 3-block feel. The fight's and walk's lengths (column.fight_ticks, carry and home times) are game lengths, not real ones (a real attack of 10 to 20 minutes would be 8 to 17 game seconds).

scouting._note: M8 step 3a, the scouts (colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Yusuf 2026): lone scouts search for termites feeding under cover, look the place over and run home laying a scent line, which the raid column follows. scout_hours: the hours scouts search, in clock hours, all day 6 to 19:30 (the user's pick 2026-11-03, so a colony finds termites sooner; night scouting in the hot season waits for the shared season source), never in the rain. hours: the raid hours, mornings 6 to 11 and evenings 16 to 19 (the paper says 16 to 19:30; raid rework R7: no raid leaves after 19:00 and one still out at 19:30, raids.hours_and_sound.dusk, turns home): a raid only leaves then, so a find made between them waits for the next raid hours (no new scouts meanwhile). A colony whose prey pile holds less than a day's food sends one scout per workers_per_scout workers (at least 1, at most most_scouts; 1 per 50 up to 5, the user's pick 2026-11-03), majors only. A scout rechecks the colony's good spots first, else searches in its own direction (raids.search: scouts search like real ants, 2026-11-04, in place of R5's slices and rings). Each scout has its own reach: first_range at first, range_step more after each trip it really searched and came home empty, up to most_range (the real foraging range, about 95 m; a block counts as a metre for distances), and just past its find after a find; the colony's reach is its scouts' farthest. It smells termites within smell blocks (out of their mound, never in it, or in their dug feeding galleries and runways), looks a find over inspect_ticks, and goes home; nothing by trip_ticks: home empty. A good spot is forgotten after spot_fade_ticks unchecked or spot_misses empty checks. Every number my pick, to confirm.
scouting._hours_note: Raid rework R7 (the user's answer, 2026-11-04): no raid leaves after 19:00, so the evening raid hours end there (the paper's 19:30 is now raids.hours_and_sound.dusk, when a raid still out turns home).
scouting._settled_range_note: R8's balance pass (2026-11-04): a settled colony, one of new land (a colony of 100 to 2,300 is years old, Yusuf 2026, and its scouts have searched this land for months), starts each new scout's reach here, the whole foraging range, not at first_range (a colony new to the place: the command's, the tests', later a split-off daughter, M9). On new land the nearest termite feeding spot is usually 60 to 90 blocks away (one termite species, mounds every 96 blocks), past what scouts starting at 32 reach before the colony starves. After a find a scout's reach still shrinks to just past it. My pick, to confirm.

choosing._note: Raid rework R5, scouts that choose (colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Real Megaponera (Frank and Linsenmair 2017, Animal Behaviour, optimal foraging in the group-hunting termite specialist): rich termite sites are raided over the whole foraging range, poor ones only near the nest, and the raid's size follows the termites the scout found; a hungry colony sends more scouts and bigger raids. A scout smells only real feeding: termites out of their mound, or a feeding gallery or runway fed at by day (termites eating there out of sight, counted as by_day_termites termites: 5 since 2026-11-08, the user's report of scouts ignoring mud-covered branches and trees; at 2 a feeding place was worth 6, too poor past 30 blocks for a fed colony, while a real Macrotermes feeding site under sheeting is a rich site raided over the whole range, and the scouts out of sight already value one 6 to 18); a bare gallery cell is no find. The look counts every feeding place within twice smell of the find (the patch it will not smell again if it passes it over). It walks up to inspect_from blocks of the find (just outside the termites' 3-block feel) and counts the termites within its smell all through its look (inspect_ticks near it), keeping the most at once; a find's worth is 3 a termite. A find is taken only if its worth reaches (least_worth + worth_per_block for each block from the nest) times a hunger factor, from hungry_ease for a starving colony to 1 for a nearly fed one; else the scout passes it over and searches on. A nearly fed colony sends fed_scouts of its scouts (rounded up), a starving one all of them. Real numbers, noted only (Frank and Linsenmair 2017, Yusuf 2026): a real colony has about 10 to 20 scouts, searching in two sessions a day, a session sometimes over an hour; the user's 1 scout per 50 workers up to 5, searching all day, are kept. Every number my pick, to confirm.

search._note: Raid scouts search like real ants (2026-11-04, the user and the parent session: R5's slices swept in neat arcs were not real; colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal, entity.ScoutMemory). Real ants: a searching forager walks a correlated random walk, each step turned a little from the last (Bell 1990, Searching Behaviour; Wehner's desert ants), and where it meets a cue of food it slows down and turns more, staying in the good patch (area-restricted search, Bell 1990); it heads home straight by path integration (Wehner 2003; well known in many ants, assumed for Megaponera); ponerine foragers keep their own favourite sector trip after trip (route and site fidelity, Fresneau 1985, Pachycondyla apicalis), widening it after empty trips and going back to where they found prey. Not measured for Megaponera scouts; every number my pick, to confirm. Each scout's own direction: a new scout takes the best of spread_tries random directions (farthest from its colony's other scouts'), saved on the ant. Out: it walks fairly straight that way, each hop turned about out_wiggle degrees, to where its search starts: out_near + (out_far - out_near) * u^out_bias of its reach for an even random u (usually near, now and then far). Search: steps of step blocks, each turned about turn degrees (a normal spread) from the last, pulled softly back once farther than stay_share of the walk out (at least stay_least blocks) from where it started, never past its reach. area_search: within scent blocks of termites feeding, a feeding gallery or runway, or a termite tunnel, it walks at pace of its pace, steps of step blocks turned about turn degrees, leaning toward of the way to the smell, for ticks after it last smelt it. Memory: a trip counts only if it searched at least searched_share of trip_ticks (the old search range bug in its new form: a scout that only set out learns nothing); an empty one grows its reach by scouting.range_step and drifts its direction about drift degrees, or, its reach already the most, swings it about swing degrees; a find turns its direction to the find and sets its reach to the find's distance plus find_margin (never under first_range).

mound_clue._note: Raid rework R6, the mound as a clue (the user's idea, 2026-11-03; colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Not described in the papers; believable, as Macrotermes feed in galleries spreading out from their mound, the feeding spots 10 to 30 blocks past its foot. A scout searching that comes within notice blocks of a living termite mound's foot (a mound the colony has not ringed lately and no other scout is ringing) searches round it in widening rings ring_step apart, the first ring_step / 2 past the foot, out to past_foot blocks past it (its smell covers the gaps); its trip is extra_ticks longer, once a trip; points past the colony's most_range are left out. A mound ringed with nothing found is left fade_ticks. A tunnel of termites going to food (a gallery out to a feeding place, or the way to a mud runway) smelt within smell blocks on the way, wherever the scout is, is followed outward, away from the mound, to its end, a point every follow_every blocks along it; what it finds there must still pass the choosing rules. Every number my pick, to confirm.

away._note: M8 step 3f, raids out of sight (colony.RaidsAway): while the colony is away (its land not loaded, or no player within 64 blocks), a hungry colony raids as numbers in the raid hours (scouting.hours), dry, at most most_raids_a_day raids a day, one at a time, to the best remembered find still worth a raid (choosing), its size as the real column's (column). Times from the distance: column.form_ticks mustering, the march out at pace blocks a second, at most fight_ticks at the spot, column.regroup_ticks, home at pace times carry.laden_pace; a raid whose attack would come after dusk does not leave. At the attack the raiders take catch.per_raider termites each (give or take a quarter, at most catch.most_catch) from the termite colony whose mound is nearest the spot within termite_reach blocks, never more than most_take_share of the real termites its workers inside stand for (its colony.stands_for; M8 step 3d), its count losing one in stands_for of them; that colony remembers the attack (its danger map: it keeps off the spot a few days and plugs the holes there). lost_share of the raiders die, hurt_share come home hurt. A find whose termites are gone or keep off it counts an empty check; a spot with a player within player_near blocks is left for real ants. Out of sight the scouts are numbers too: in the scouting hours, hungry and knowing no find worth a raid, each scout the colony would send has scout_find_chance an hour to find one of the termites' feeding places within its reach that it does not know yet (nearer ones likelier), worth scout_worth_least to scout_worth_most. Real Megaponera raid 1 to 4 times a day, 30 to 75 percent of the colony (Yusuf 2026). M8 step 3e: most_raids_a_day is the colony's whole day, near or away (real columns count too), and the hungrier the colony the more it wants: 1 when nearly fed up to most_raids_a_day with an empty pile (commands do not count). Every number my pick, to confirm.

catch._note: M8 step 3d, the termites' losses (colony.RaidCatch; the user's pick 2026-11-06, 'count stands for many'). Real raids carry home about 200 to 1,000 termites with 150 to 550 ants, a few an ant (majors 1 to 12, minors 1 to 3; Yusuf 2026, Table 1). The raiders who go as numbers (and every raider of a raid out of sight) bring home per_raider termites each, give or take a quarter, from the termites feeding under the mud at the spot (numbers in the termite colony's galleries), only if the termite colony still feeds there; at most most_catch a raid; the termite colony's count loses one in its stands_for of them, and it keeps off the spot a few days. The real raiders carry the real termites they sting, as before. No raid is bigger than most_raid ants (real raiding parties up to about 500). Every number my pick, to confirm.

hours_and_sound._note: Raid rework R7, hours and sound (colony.Raids, colony.RaidColumn). Raids end by dusk (the user's answer, 2026-11-04): no raid leaves after 19:00 (the evening raid hours in scouting.hours end there: time to reach a spot and come home), a raid still out at dusk (19:30) stops where it is, picks up what it stung and walks home, and until the morning's first raid hour (6:00) it stays dusk, so a find made after 19:00 waits for the morning. Rare night raids in the hot season (Yusuf 2026) wait for the shared season source (Serene Seasons, M9). A raid a command sends outside the raid hours (/antcolonies raid, /antcolonies scout anytime) keeps no hours. The attack: once no termite has been about the spot (within carry.collect_reach) for quiet_ticks, the attack is over (real raids: the attack at the feeding site lasts about 10 to 20 minutes, the termites stung, fled or sealed in; Yusuf 2026; column.fight_ticks is the most it may last). The squeak (Hoelldobler et al. 1994: the columns' stridulation is no message between the ants but a warning to big animals): the raider nearest a player within squeak_hear blocks squeaks, squeak_quiet loud every squeak_every_far ticks at that distance, up to squeak_loud every squeak_every_near ticks at squeak_loud_at blocks, before anyone stings. A column marching into land not ticking within edge_look blocks ahead of its front turns home at that edge (until drawn-only ants, M8 step 4). Every number my pick, to confirm.

column._note: M8 step 3b, the raid column (colony.RaidColumn, MatabeleRaidGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Hoelldobler et al. 1994, Frank et al. 2017-2018, Yusuf 2026): the scout home from a find recruits nestmates at the entrance and leads them out along its scent line; the raid's size follows what the scout found (Frank 2018), 30 to 75 percent of the colony (Yusuf 2026). M8 step 3d: the raid takes the share of the workers the colony can spare, least_share (a fed colony) to most_share (a starving one), all of it for a find worth rich_worth or more (a by-day feeding place, or 2 termites seen; a termite is worth 3), a part for a poorer find, at least least_raid, at most catch.most_raid; at most most_real walk as real ants, the rest are numbers till step 4. The scout leads off as soon as it has called; a raider still in the nest form_ticks after the column left stays home. The march (the ribbon, the user's pick of 2026-11-07): rows spacing blocks apart, abreast side by side and one fewer by turns, nobody stopping on the way. It stops stop_short blocks before the find and bunches up (at most gather_ticks), then every ant attacks at once (majors break the mud open, minors go in; the termite workers first, soldiers only in the way), at most fight_ticks; then they regroup there (at most regroup_ticks) and walk home along the trail as a column, every ant home or let go after home_ticks. Every number my pick, to confirm.
column._spacing_note: Real sizes, step 2 (docs/plans/real-sizes.md): 0.6 blocks between ants (was 1.2), a little over one major's length (0.5) nose to nose, about real for a marching Megaponera column, the ants almost touching. The gap look 4, gap stop 1.5, stop_short 4 and the spread 8 stay: they are distances on the ground (a block a metre). My pick, to confirm.
column._ribbon_note: The ribbon (the user's pick of 2026-11-07, march viewer formation B with exit 2): the scout runs down into the nest, calls there and comes out first (the user's plan of 2026-11-08), leading 5 percent faster than the column (RaidColumn's FRONT_PACE; raiders already outside wait for it by the entrance, the ones inside gather by the foot of its shaft and climb out behind it at a walk, then hurry to their places at up to 1.6; on the way out, up the shaft and down the hump, raiders climb about as fast as they walk, RaidColumn's MARCH_CLIMB, the user's offer of 2026-11-08); rows of abreast and one fewer by turns, spacing apart, each ant in its own lane; nobody stops while marching. A raider still in the nest form_ticks after the column left stays home. (single_file, stretch and least_form_ticks, the old march, removed 2026-11-07.)
column._single_file_note: Raid flow (the user's raid of 2026-11-06, the column peeling off one ant at a time): single file only for the first single_file blocks from the entrance, two abreast for as many again, then abreast; was 8. Real columns are a band 1 to 3 ants wide from the nest on (Longhurst and Howse 1979). My pick, to confirm.
column._fight_ticks_note: Raid rework R7: the attack's longest, 2 minutes (was 5; the raid diary's attacks ran about 4 minutes, a raid out from 8:00 to 14:00 in game hours). Most attacks now end sooner, quiet_ticks after the last termite about (raids.hours_and_sound). My pick, to confirm.

carry._note: M8 step 3c, home with the prey (colony.RaidColumn, BringPreyGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Yusuf 2026): after the fight the raiders gather the stung termites, a major holding a bundle of up to about 12 under its jaws, a minor 1 to 3, and walk home as a column; the prey is eaten in the nest. A worker holds least_major (the shortest drawn as a major) to most_major (the longest major), least_minor to most_minor for a minor, by its length. The raiders pick up the paralysed termites within collect_reach blocks of the find, workers before soldiers, at most collect_ticks, each pick-up pick_ticks. A raid that found nothing spreads round the spot up to spread_reach blocks for spread_ticks, a raider seeing a termite within spread_see blocks going for it, then gathers what it stung; still nothing: home, and the find counts an empty check. Laden, the column walks home at laden_pace of its pace. At home each carrier lays its termites on the prey pile, termites_per_layer to a layer (one that finds no way to the pile in bring_ticks has them laid there out of sight). A raider that leaves the column hurt (crippled, or a soldier clamped on a leg) follows the raid's trail home alone, at most limp_ticks. Every number my pick, to confirm, but the loads (real).

trails._note: M8 raid rework R4, the scent trails (colony.ScentTrails). Real Megaponera lay their trail from the poison gland, every raider on the way out (so the way home does not hang on the scout), and it lasts up to about 29 hours (Hoelldobler et al. 1994; a game day counted as a real day, so 29,000 ticks). A trail a raid column walked lasts lasting_ticks after it was last walked; a lone scout's line, weaker, scout_lasting_ticks; a later raid to the same spot follows a trail still smelt, and with the trail gone and the scout dead nobody knows the way. A trail is broken where a block is dug or put on it or water covers it: the column stops at the gap and the front ants cast about at least cast_ticks, plus cast_per_block for each block of the gap; a far side within cast_reach blocks is picked up and the gap mended with new scent; a wider gap, after cast_give_ticks, is crossed only if a former scout walks in the column (it leads on from memory, a hypothesis in AntWiki, never tested), else the raid turns home (the way home is always found). Every number my pick, to confirm, but the 29 hours.

defence._note: M8 step 2e, the player (the user's calls, 2026-10-25; fight.NestDefence, fight.DefenceNumbers). Real Megaponera sting anyone who breaks into the nest or treads on a raid column, a sting among the most painful of any ant, and squeak loudly as they do. A player provokes the colony by breaking its nest (a block within nest_radius of the entrance or of a room), hitting a member, standing in a column (touching a fighting ant column_touch_ticks, 1 s) or staying on the nest (look: walking within radius of the entrance brings ants out to look, who sting if the player stays sting_after ticks, 3 s, then go in after lasts).
